disambiguation.justification: Every tool has a distinct read or write role, and the descriptions cross-reference each other explicitly, e.g. search_transactions for records versus summarize_transactions for totals and run_query as the bounded escape hatch. The get_context versus list_entities split is likewise stated outright, leaving no enforceable ambiguity.

naming_consistency.justification: All names follow verb_noun in lower snake_case: get_context, list_entities, search_transactions, summarize_transactions, run_query, and a uniform manage_<domain> family for writes. Action variants are consolidated inside each tool rather than producing inconsistent per-action names.

tool_count_appropriateness.justification: Fifteen tools for a budget domain spanning accounts, transactions, categories, payees, tags, rules, schedules, budget months and files is well-scoped. Broad operations are folded into action parameters, so no tool feels redundant.

completeness.justification: The surface covers the full lifecycle: reading structure and entities, searching and summarizing transactions, CRUD for every entity kind, budget month and file management, plus a SQL escape hatch for gaps. No obvious dead ends remain for the stated purpose.

summary: A highly coherent tool set: crisp verb_noun naming, explicit boundaries between read tools and between the manage_ write tools, and full lifecycle coverage of the Actual Budget domain. At fifteen well-consolidated tools it is neither thin nor bloated, and no supplied shadow candidates apply.
